The paper investigates the local crystallographic structure of ferromagnetic Ga_yFe_4-yN nanocrystals embedded in GaN.
A combination of anomalous x-ray diffraction and diffraction anomalous fine structure was used to study the local crystallographic structure.
Ga atoms occupy 3c sites in the fcc structure of the nanocrystals.
The amount of Ga in 3c sites increases with the normalized Ga-flow.
The magnetic response of the embedded nanocrystals is ferromagnetic with a Curie temperature increasing from 450K to 500K with the Ga occupation.
The maximum occupancy of Ga atoms in 3c sites is 30%.
The lattice parameter of the NCs along the c-growth direction increases with decreasing normalized Ga-flow.
The size of the nanocrystals is limited to (17±8)nm along the c-growth direction.
The density of the nanocrystals is tuneable by the amount of Ga provided during growth.
The Curie temperature of the ferromagnetic nanocrystals increases from 450K to 500K with the Ga occupation.
The paper demonstrates the potential of the DAFS method for unravelling the local structure of magnetic phase-separated systems.
The results show that the Ga atoms in 3c sites have a unique Ga-N distance R of 1.983±0.033 ˚A.
The results show that the Ga atoms in 3c sites have a unique Ga-Fe distance R of 2.856±0.127 ˚A.
The results show that the Ga atoms in 3c sites have a unique Ga-Ga distance R of 2.799±0.083 ˚A.
The results show that the Debye-Waller factor σ2 for the Ga-N distance is 0.0115±0.0000 10^(-3) ˚A^2.
The results show that the Debye-Waller factor σ2 for the Ga-Fe distance is 0.0151±0.0027 10^(-3) ˚A^2.
The results show that the Debye-Waller factor σ2 for the Ga-Ga distance is 0.0135±0.0024 10^(-3) ˚A^2.
